emma: heads-up — canary (2% traffic) for release/2026-03-18 caused a small spike of 503s tied to long-lived KV prefixes. I rolled the canary back but want a safe post-rollback procedure so clients aren't left in a bad state. asking: sequence for traffic migration + cache/key invalidation + node drain?

raj: ok, high level I'd do: 1) stop new canary traffic (move split to baseline) 2) mark canary nodes as `draining` so they finish inflight requests 3) evict or shadow-delete problematic KV prefixes with a TTL bump 4) once inflight done, detach and kill canary tasks 5) monitor telemetry for error/regression for 30m. Keep it staged, don't mass-delete keys.

joel: agree. add: before evicting, write a compatibility shim that returns 200+safe payload for clients expecting the old key. helps avoid hammering fallback logic.

emma: can you paste the exact commands for eviction/drain? I want a runbook entry.

raj: sure, quick examples — these are idempotent: 
```
# mark nodes draining
redwood infra set-node-state --pool canary --state draining --reason "canary rollback"

# graceful stop (waits for inflight)
redwood infra drain --node <id> --timeout 300

# evict prefix (safe: schedule background TTL bump then delete)
redwood kv ttl-bump --prefix "session:exp:2026-03" --ttl 60
sleep 60
redwood kv delete-prefix --prefix "session:exp:2026-03" --batch-size 500
```

raj: note: prefer TTL bump then delete so we don't create a vacuum of missing keys that upstreams interpret as error. if keys are huge, do delete in small batches and watch RPS on KV service.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollback initiated by emma — traffic rebalanced to baseline pool, nodes marked draining (2/4).

sara: telemetry checklist to watch during and after: 1) 5xx rate by route 2) tail latency P99 3) kv hit/miss ratio 4) error budget burn 5) client-side retry rate. set alerts at low thresholds for the canary window.

emma: on the Console/rollouts UX side, we should expose a single "safe revert" action that orchestrates the steps above (flip split -> drain -> evict prefix with configured strategy). currently operators have to run 4 different tools.

joel: +1. I'd propose the API shape: `POST /internal/rollouts/{id}/revert?mode=safe|fast&kv_mode=ttl_bump|delete|noop` returns an operation id. fast would just flip traffic and kill; safe does the drain + kv strategy. must be idempotent.

raj: also add a guard on fast revert: only allow if error rate > X and no ongoing migration flags. otherwise force safe. we burned a lot of client retries last time with naive fast kills.

emma: good point — we should make the Console default to safe for canaries <10% traffic and surface the fast option behind a confirmation.

sara: update dashboards: add a temporary per-rollout panel (7m granularity) that shows split by user cohort, KV error ratio per prefix, and inflight count per node. that will make it obvious when to run the eviction.

joel: for A/B experiments we also need to preserve assignment mapping on rollback. otherwise users flip cohorts and we get noise in metrics. include a `preserve_assignment=true` flag in revert API.

raj: operational runbook snippet for Pager duty/responses: 
- step 0: page @oncall if 5xx > 0.5% for 5m
- step 1: `rollouts revert --id <id> --mode safe` (or Console button)
- step 2: watch telemetry for 15m; if errors persist, escalate and consider KV prefix manual investigation

emma: can someone draft a short runbook PR? I'll own the Console UX ticket.

joel: I'll open the API PR w/ shape + tests.

raj: I'll add CLI tools and the `kv ttl-bump`/delete safe sequence to infra repo.

sara: I'll add the dashboard panels and a low-threshold alert for the rollout job.

emma: thanks all. after we verify dashboards + API I'll drop a short note in #product and the SRE runbook. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: log — rollback-runbook-draft created by raj in infra/runbooks (link: https://git.internal/r/infra/runbooks/rollback-safe).
